newsitem.title: CHINA: Air Mauritius plans HK-Shanghai service.
newsitem.headline: Air Mauritius plans HK-Shanghai service.

text.p: Air Mauritius has been given the green light from the Chinese government to begin flying from Hong Kong to Shanghai, the airline's Hong Kong manager Cyril Gordon said.
The carrier is now applying for government permission from Hong Kong's Special Administrative Region to begin the twice weekly service next June, he told Reuters in an interview.

The extension to the existing twice weekly service between Mauritius and Hong Kong will coincide with the introduction of a Airbus A340 carrying 301passengers on at least one of the frequencies currently operated by a 181 seat Boeing 767.
"Planning is in the initial stages but we have the green light from China and now it all depends on the Hong Kong authorities," Gordon told Reuters.
The A340 will also carry around 17 tonnes of belly cargo compared to around eight tonnes on the B767.
"We never have enough space aboard the 767. At the moment we have to send cargo via Singapore, Perth and Melbourne to get round the problem," Gordon said.
Air Mauritius operates the route in a 50/50 joint venture with Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd.
The start of the Shanghai routing will also coincide with a marketing campaign to attract more Chinese passengers and cargo, the Gordon said.

He added that Mauritius is not a "designated" tourism destination for Chinese nationals but increasingly Chinese executives and diplomats are using his airline, some as transit passengers to Africa, Madagascar and the Seychelles.

Air Mauritius also benefits from Hong Kong garment manufacturers who have factories in Mauritius using belly space to transport raw materials. - Reuters Air Cargo Service Tel+ 44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017 - www.racs.com
